c1.note: The SDNY/DOJ release confirms the Dec 6 2019 DPA, the $520,650,432 penalty including $9.52M for Ericsson Egypt, the 3-year monitor, and the five countries. Every variant is consistent with this.

c2.note: Ericsson Egypt pleaded guilty on Dec 6 2019 to conspiracy to violate the FCPA anti-bribery provisions.

c3.note: The SEC settlement of Dec 6 2019 totalled $539.92M: $458.38M disgorgement plus $81.54M prejudgment interest. The $427M of business and the countries match the SEC release.

c4.note: Stanford FCPA Clearinghouse confirms the June 17 2016 disclosure, the SEC start in 2013, the DOJ start in 2015, and the SEK 12bn accrual in the Sept 2019 6-K.

c5.note: OCCRP reported on May 22 2013 that the SEC had opened an inquiry tied to Thomas Lundin's Romania slush-fund allegations.

c6.note: Ekot reported on 23 Nov 2016 a SEK 2.5M payment in 1999 to a Panama account linked to Rodríguez, who denies receiving bribes. It is an allegation only.

c7.note: Ericsson's 7 Jul 2017 release says two current and four former employees were indicted over the 1999 Ericsson Microwave Systems radar contract.

c8.note: Ekot reported on 22 Jan 2020 that the former Ericsson executives were acquitted of bribery in Greece, while Greek intermediaries were convicted of money laundering. The passage names Broberg and Bertil Hellström rather than Kurt Hellström, so that detail is not confirmed by it.

c9.note: The indictment was filed on June 30 2020 and unsealed on Sept 8 2021, charging an FCPA and money-laundering conspiracy over about $2.1M in Djibouti bribes. No disposition is verified.

c10.note: Ericsson's press release of Oct 21 2021 (Oct 22 in Stockholm) discloses the DOJ's DPA breach determination. Variant E dates the determination Oct 22, which is a minor discrepancy.

c11.note: ICIJ and about 30 media partners reported in Feb 2022 on the Iraq suspicious payments, the ISIS permission and the Speedway route. Ericsson said no payments to terrorist organisations were identified.

c12.note: On March 1 2022 the DOJ told Ericsson its pre-DPA Iraq disclosure was insufficient and that its failure to make later disclosures breached the DPA. Ericsson disclosed this on Mar 2.

c13.note: The SEC opened its Iraq investigation in June 2022. On Sept 26 2024 SEC staff said it had concluded and did not intend to recommend enforcement. The 2019 injunction remains.

c14.note: Solna District Court acquitted four former Ericsson executives on June 21 2022 because prosecutors did not prove the money was received.

c15.note: DN, citing Sveriges Radio, reported on 2024-01-10 that Svea hovrätt upheld the acquittals of the four former Ericsson employees in the Djibouti case.

c16.note: Ericsson's Q3 2026 report confirms the August 2022 D.D.C. Anti-Terrorism Act suit against the Ericsson entities, Ekholm and a former employee. It is still pending.

c17.note: The February 2024 second suit is confirmed, and the later suits are stayed pending the dismissal motions in the earlier-filed case.

c18.note: The annual report confirms a November 2025 third suit (France, Afghanistan, Belgium), stayed pending the earlier suit's dismissal motions.

c19.note: The Q3 2026 report confirms a fourth suit filed in March 2026 against the same defendants.

c20.note: A fifth Anti-Terrorism Act suit was filed in D.D.C. in September 2026, per the Q3 2026 report.

c21.note: The Swedish Prosecution Authority's October 2022 release closed the Kuwait and Iraq inquiries. The exact day and the USD 450k figure rest on what I recall rather than the passage.

c22.note: The Swedish prosecutor closed the China probe on 2022-11-14 for lack of evidence, and the Kuwait and Iraq probes had already been dropped.

c23.note: Ericsson's 2022-12-14 press release says it agreed with the DOJ and SEC to extend the monitor by one year, to June 2024.

c24.note: On 2023-03-02 the DOJ announced Ericsson agreed to plead guilty and pay USD 206,728,848. The plea itself was entered 2023-03-21, so A and C overstate by saying it pleaded on March 2.

c25.note: Ericsson pleaded guilty on 2023-03-21 in SDNY, with a USD 206.7m additional penalty. The judgment was signed 2023-03-30, so D's sentencing date of 03-21 is wrong.

c26.note: EDNY dismissed the shareholder securities suit with prejudice on 2023-05-24, per Ericsson's 25 May release; the Second Circuit affirmed later.

c27.note: Ericsson's Q3 2024 filing states the Second Circuit affirmed the dismissal on 2024-09-03.

c28.note: 93 funded claimants sued in Solna from August 2023 over Iraq-report disclosure. The Supreme Court refused leave to appeal on 2026-03-12 and the merits have resumed.

c29.note: The monitorship and plea agreement ended on 2024-06-02. Ericsson announced it on June 3, so F's announcement date is off by a day, and Ericsson continues to cooperate with DOJ and SEC on historical conduct.

c30.note: The Q3 2026 report lists the DOJ Iraq-related investigation under governmental proceedings. I could not see the full text, so the Syria expansion and the ongoing status rest partly on the other systems' agreement and what I recall.

c31.note: Goldman Sachs 1MDB DPA is a different company and was correctly excluded; the passages concern Ericsson's own DPA, not Goldman's.

c32.note: Ericsson Inc. is a fully owned US-incorporated operating subsidiary, a separate legal entity from the parent.

c33.note: Ericsson Egypt pleaded guilty in Dec 2019 as a subsidiary while the parent got the DPA. The exclusion is accurate, although the plea is part of the same enforcement action.

c34.note: Erickson Inc. is an Oregon aviation company, unrelated to Ericsson; correctly excluded.

c35.note: Sony Ericsson was a separate JV, now wholly owned by Sony, and has no link to the bribery matters; the exclusion is sound.

c36.note: The SAMR probe into patent licensing opened April 2019 and is still open per the Q3 2026 report. It is antitrust, not bribery, so exclusion is right.

c37.note: No passage supports a Nokia claim settlement. Ericsson and Nokia did settle a dispute around 2021, but I recall it as relating to a patent or other matter, not the FCPA events, and the $97M/€80M figure is not supported.
